text.gross:
Can involve any area of the CNS (no predilection for gray or white matter)
• Nerve roots may also be involved
• Foci of hemorrhage and necrosis, which may progress to granular, yellow-brown to gray foci
text.dx:
Working identification: Toxocara canis cerebrospinal migration.
Obligate intracellular protozoan. CNS infection targets neurons and astrocytes. 
In utero infections likely to result in the CNS infection. 

Specimen site: Brain / spinal cord / meninges. 
Formulate the final morphologic diagnosis from the visible tissue, distribution, severity and process; etiology requires supporting evidence.
text.histo:
Protozoa are seen targeting neurons and astrocytes
Hemorrhage and necrosis
text.why: Host: Dogs in the lecture list. Mechanism: Aberrant CNS migration may injure neural tissue and vessels.
text.notes:
This parasite targets different cell types. Parasitizes variety of cell types (lungs, lymphoid system, liver, heart, skeletal muscle, pancreas,
gastrointestinal (GI) tract, eyes, and nervous system)
• CNS infection targets neurons and astrocytes

In mature animals, T. gondii infections have been associated with immunosuppression, like canine distempter virus.
